newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia says new Cambodian PM an internal affair.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia says new Cambodian PM an internal affair.

text.p: Indonesian Foreign Minister Ali Alatas said the election of Ung Huot as Cambodia's new first prime minister was an internal affair of that country, the official Antara news agency reported on Friday.

"The recognition or non-recognition of Ung Huot as Cambodia's first prime minister is nothing to Indonesia because Indonesia's recognition applies only to the state, not the government of Cambodia," Alatas was quoted as saying at an ASEAN function on Thursday night.
Foreign ministers of the Association of South East Asian Nations (ASEAN) will meet in Singapore on Monday to discuss the appointment of Ung Huot, who is also Cambodia's foreign minister.
Second Prime Minister and strongman Hun Sen ousted the previous first prime minister, Prince Norodom Ranariddh, in a coup in early July.
The move brought international condemnation and pushed ASEAN into postponing Cambodia's admittance to the organisation it was due to have joined together with Burma and Laos late last month.

Alatas declined to comment on ASEAN's attitude to Ung Huot's election by the Cambodian parliament on Wednesday. More than two-thirds of Cambodia's National Assembly members voted by secret ballot to accept Ung Huot's nomination as first prime minister.
"We must wait until after a ministerial meeting in Singapore on Monday," he said.
The United States has said it will deal with Ung Huot, even though it considers the process of his selection undemocratic.

Alatas heads an ASEAN mediation team including the foreign ministers of Thailand and the Philippines seeking an end to the crisis in Cambodia, one of the group's major challenges as it celebrates its 30th anniversary.
The three ministers saw Hun Sen in Phnom Penh last Saturday and are also due to report on the meeting to their colleagues in Singapore.
ASEAN groups Brunei, Burma, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
